thread.title: Stocks Slip On Apple Doubts; Dow Jones Holds Support | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Slip On Apple Doubts; Dow Jones Holds Support | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks dived into early losses Monday, as Apple ( AAPL ) pulled down Dow Jones industrials and the stock market slid into a holiday-interrupted trading week.
X Dow Jones stock Apple swung nearly 2% lower after news reports said the company cut production orders for its new iPhone. Apple's news rippled across the chip sector. Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ), Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Micron Technologies ( MU ) led the early declines. News reports linked Micron to a probe of antitrust violations by the Chinese government. Meanwhile, Denver-based oil producer Resolute Energy ( REN ) spiked on takeover news.
A handful of China names delivered early reports, sending JD.com ( JD ) sharply lower. Intuit ( INTU ) heads up the companies due to report after the close.
Apple traded down hard and rising issues were thin on the Dow Jones industrial average, sending the index down 0.2% in opening trade. The S&P 500 also dropped 0.2%, with PG&E ( PCG ) and Cimarex Energy ( XEC ) leading its declines.
The Nasdaq Composite slumped 0.4%, as Nvidia and JD.com spearhead the losses, and Facebook ( FB ) veered sharply lower.

Please contact customer service CLOSE While the Nasdaq and S&P 500 remain below key levels of support, the Dow Jones industrials has a two-day rebound under its belt , suggesting some support at its 200-day line. The index starts the week 1.3% above that line, which has flattened out just above the 25,000 level. Trading on the stock market is likely to be lighter than usual this week due to the Thanksgiving holiday week.
Apple Cuts iPhone Production; Facebook Dives Apple dropped 2.4% in opening trade. The company "slashed production orders" for all three of the new iPhone models introduced in September, the Wall Street Journal reported . Lower-than-forecast demand and the multiple-model release led to confusion in the company's supply chain, particularly with regard to its iPhone XR.
Apple shares ended Friday narrowly below support at their 200-day moving average, a line below which the stock has not spent more than five days at a time since 2016.
FANG stocks stumbled lower in early trade. Facebook tumbled 2.5%, Amazon.com ( AMZN ) posted a 2% loss. Facebook is now trading down 38% from its July record, and at its lowest mark since March 2017.
PG&E crumbled 8%, after the company disclosed a second power line failure occurred on the morning that California's Camp Fire disaster began . Downed power lines are one potential cause being investigated in the fire which has caused 77 known deaths. PG&E shares are down 54% since the Nov. 8 start of the fire.
Breakout Watch: Tesla, Ulta Beauty, PRA Health Tesla ( TSLA ) rose 1.2% in early action. That lifted the stock just above a 357.67 buy point in a four-month, cup-with-handle base.
PRA Health Sciences ( PRAH ) traded 0.8% lower at the open. The provider of pharmaceutical clinical trial services is below a 108.32 buy point in a cup-with-handle base.
On the IBD 50 list, Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) grabbed an early lead, up 1.4%. The IBD Leaderboard stock broke out past a 290.40 buy point Nov. 8. It is trading just beyond buy range, and is testing resistance at the level of its prior high, established in June 2o17.
Resolute Energy rattled off an early11% gain, rising after Cimarex Energy ( XEC ) agreed to buy the oil producer for about $900 million. Both companies are based in Denver. Cimarex shares dropped 4% in early trade.
Nat Gas Heads For Biggest Month Since '09; Oil Prices Slip Oil prices reversed early gains to trade lower, while natural gas prices were still volatile in early trade. West Texas Intermediate fell 1.4% to $55.67 a barrel. That is down more than 14% for November, steering oil toward its worst monthly decline since July 2015.
Natural gas rose 4% in early trade, to $4.45 per million British thermal units. Up 38% since Nov. 1, gas prices are tracking toward their strongest monthly advance in nearly a decade.
Monday's economic calendar is thin, with the National Association of Homebuilders' November housing market index due out at 10 a.m. ET. New York Federal Reserve President John Williams has a busy speaking schedule for the day, joining in public discussions in New York at 9:40 a.m., 10:45 a.m. and 3:15 p.m. ET.
European Trade Turns Mixed, China Rises Brexit issues remained center-stage in Europe, where markets slipped into mixed action in afternoon trade as British Prime Minister Theresa May continued to press her EU disengagement plan in the face of steep opposition. London's FTSE 100 added tightened its early gain to 0.3%, while Frankfurt's DAX fell 0.2% and the CAC-40 in Paris dipped 0.1%.
Stock markets in China climbed Monday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index gained 0.7%. The Shanghai Composite jumped 0.9%, enough to retake the 2,700 level as it attempts to form a bottom in its nine-month pullback. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 snatched a 0.7% gain.
